result.summary: The street features a well-maintained pedestrian environment with continuous sidewalks and a buffered bike lane that narrows the vehicle travel lane. The presence of street trees and flexible bollards provides a degree of vertical separation and visual interest, though no marked pedestrian crossings are visible in the immediate mid-block area.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated pedestrian crossing points visible along this stretch of the street, which may lead to unsafe mid-block crossings.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk to provide a designated space for pedestrians to cross the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Implement a raised crosswalk to act as a speed table, slowing vehicle traffic and prioritizing pedestrian movement.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a narrow sidewalk along a row of residential buildings, featuring a green painted bike lane adjacent to the curb. The walkway is in poor condition with significant cracking, uneven surfaces, and obstructions including a large tree and utility pole that restrict the clear path.

hazards.name: Uneven and cracked sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface is severely degraded with large cracks and uneven slabs, creating significant tripping hazards.

hazards.name: Fixed obstructions
hazards.description: A large tree trunk and a utility pole significantly narrow the effective walking width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the sidewalk

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repave and level the sidewalk to provide a smooth, ADA-compliant surface free of tripping hazards.

interventions.title: Tree Pit Expansion
interventions.description: Enlarge the tree pit or install permeable pavers to accommodate root growth without buckling the sidewalk surface.

interventions.title: Clear Path Maintenance
interventions.description: Ensure a consistent clear walking width by managing encroachments from stairs and planters.

result.summary: The image shows a well-equipped urban street with high-visibility continental crosswalks, wide sidewalks, and a dedicated green-painted bike lane. The environment includes pedestrian signals and curb ramps with tactile paving, though sightlines are partially obscured by parked vehicles near the intersection.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corner block the sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the foreground intersection near the red fire hydrant.

hazards.name: Lack of Physical Bike Lane Protection
hazards.description: The bike lane is only separated by paint and flexible bollards, which may not prevent vehicle encroachment.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove the parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to slow vehicle speeds and increase pedestrian prominence.

interventions.title: Hardened Centerline/Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install physical barriers or extend the curb to further reduce turning speeds and shorten crossing distances.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, paved sidewalk in good condition, but it is bordered by a long stretch of blank, boarded-up building frontage. While a marked crosswalk is visible, the lack of street trees, lighting, and active ground-floor uses creates a sterile and potentially unsafe-feeling environment at night.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The boarded-up building creates a lack of natural surveillance ('eyes on the street'), which can decrease perceived and actual safety for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and background, the brick building with boarded windows.

hazards.name: Lack of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No street lighting is visible in the immediate vicinity, which poses a safety risk for pedestrians after dark.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large black utility box or trash receptacle is placed in the middle of the sidewalk area, narrowing the clear path.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lamps to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Introduce vegetation to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway and to improve the aesthetic quality of the walk.

interventions.title: Frontage Activation
interventions.description: Encourage the rehabilitation of the boarded-up building to include active ground-floor uses or transparent windows to improve natural surveillance.
